title: Revisiting lattice dynamics and stability of lead-free double perovskites Cs2InAgX6 (X = F, Br, Cl) from first-principles calculations

segments.text: Halide double perovskites are promising candidates for optoelectronic and thermoelectric applications due to their tunable structural, electronic, and vibrational properties.
However, achieving an accurate description of these properties remains a challenge within density functional theory.
The structural, electronic, mechanical, and vibrational properties of Cs2InAgX6 (X = F, Cl, Br) are investigated using the PBEsol and HSE06 functionals.

The computed lattice parameters increase systematically with halide ionic size, consistent with experimental trends, while elastic constants satisfy the Born stability criteria and decrease from fluoride to bromide, indicating progressively weaker bonding.
Bandgap energies show an increasing trend with halogen electronegativity due to changes in orbital hybridization, and HSE06 results agree well with available experimental data.
Born effective charges and dielectric constants reveal a strong halide dependence of polarization response, with the bromide compound exhibiting the largest values.

Detailed phonon calculations, including symmetry-resolved mode assignment and dispersion relations, indicate that Cs2InAgCl6 and Cs2InAgF6 are dynamically stable, while Cs2InAgBr6 displays soft modes consistent with experimentally observed phase transitions; notably, the predicted stability of the fluoride compound contrasts with several previous density functional theory reports.

These findings highlight the critical role of the halide element in the governance of bonding, electronic structure, and stability and identify Cs2InAgCl6 and Cs2InAgF6 as promising stable materials for optoelectronic applications.

title: Carbon Nanotube Yarns Tailored Using Dispersants and Surfactants for Flexible and Wearable Thermoelectric Generators

segments.text: Carbon nanotube (CNT) yarns have emerged as a promising candidate for flexible and fabric-type wearable thermoelectric devices.
This study developed CNT yarns tailored by a low-cost, fast, and environmentally friendly CNT dispersion method using glycerol as a dispersant and polyoxyethylene(50) stearyl ether as a surfactant.
A high power factor of 242 mu W m(-1) K-2 was obtained, which is ca. three times higher than that of the previous dispersion method.

The significant contribution is the 2-fold increase of electrical conductivity (from 325 to 747 S cm(-1)), which originates from the higher degree of disentanglement in dispersion and better CNT alignment in the yarn.
Another contribution is the suppression of the increase in thermal conductivity as a possible side effect of the CNT alignment, which is concluded to be due to the surfactant adsorbed on CNT bundles.
As a result, the figure of merit ZT value was successfully improved by ca. a factor of 3.

title: Soret Effect of Ionic Liquid Gels for Thermoelectric Conversion

segments.text: Cations and anions can accumulate at the two ends of an ionic conductor under temperature gradient, which is the so-called Soret effect.
This can generate a voltage between the two electrodes, and the thermopower can be higher than that of the electronic conductors because of the Seebeck effect by 1-2 orders in magnitude.
The thermoelectric properties of ionic conductors depend on the ionic thermopower, ionic conductivity, and thermal conductivity.
Compared with other ionic conductors, like liquid electrolytes and hydrogels, ionogels made of an ionic liquid and a gelator can have the advantages of high thermopower and high stability.
Great progress was recently made to improve the ionic conductivity and/or ionic thermopower of ionogels.
They can be used in ionic thermoelectric capacitors (ITECs) to harvest heat.
In addition, they can be integrated with electronic thermoelectric materials to harvest heat from both temperature gradient and temperature fluctuation, which can be caused by waste heat.

title: Highly Stretchable PU Ionogels with Self-Healing Capability for a Flexible Thermoelectric Generator

segments.text: With the development of thermoelectric (TE) generator, the flexible, stretchable, self-healable, and wearable TE devices have aroused great interest.

Therefore, we designed a self-healable and stretchable polyurethane (PU) ionogel, composed of polyurethane main chains with double bonds in the side, cross-linkers (BDB) and nonconjugated ionic liquids (EMIM:DCA).
The PU ionogels with 30 wt % ILs have a high mechanical stretchability (300%), good tensile strength (1.61 MPa), and suitable Young's modulus (0.79 MPa).
The proposed materials also exhibited an excellent ionic figure of merit (ZT(i)) of 0.99 +/- 0.3, as well as rapid self-healability in the absence of any external stimuli.
The thermoelectric capability of PU ionogels kept stable under the severe condition (50% strain) and during self-healing process, which is rarely reported in recent studies.
Furthermore, a stretchable and self-healable ionic thermoelectric capacitor device is also fabricated by the PU ionogels, which can efficiently convert heat into electricity.

title: Strong anharmonicity and high thermoelectric performance of cubic thallium-based fluoride perovskites TlXF3 (X = Hg, Sn, Pb)

segments.text: State-of-the-art first-principles calculations are performed to investigate the thermoelectric transport properties in thallium-based fluoride perovskites TlXF3 (X = Hg, Sn, Pb) by considering anharmonic renormalization of the phonon energy and capturing reasonable electron relaxation times.
The lattice thermal conductivity, kappa(L), of the three compounds is very low, among which TlPbF3 is only 0.42 W m(-1) K-1 at 300 K, which is less than half of that of quartz glass.
The low acoustic mode group velocity and strong three-phonon scattering caused by the strong anharmonicity of the Tl atom are the origin of the ultralow kappa(L).
Meanwhile, the strong ionic bonds between X (X = Hg, Sn, Pb) and F atoms provide good electrical transport properties.
The results show that the ZT value of TlHgF3 at 900 K is 1.58, which is higher than the 1.5 value of FeNbSb at 1200 K.
TlSnF3 and TlPbF3 also exceed 1, which is close to the classical thermoelectric material PbTe:Na.
Furthermore, we present the methods and expected effects of improving the ZT value through nanostructures.

title: Insights into the physical properties of NaGeH3 perovskite hydride for hydrogen storage applications: A first-principles study

segments.text: Hydride perovskites have recently attracted considerable attention in the field of hydrogen storage due to their promising energy-related properties.

In this work, first-principles calculations within the framework of density functional theory (DFT) are performed to explore the structural, hydrogen storage, mechanical, electronic, and thermoelectric characteristics of the novel perovskite-type hydride NaGeH3.
This compound is found to crystallize in a cubic structure with an equilibrium lattice parameter of 3.98 & Aring;.
The calculated negative formation energy of-0.83 eV/atom confirms its thermodynamic stability.
Hydrogen storage evaluations reveal that NaGeH3 offers a gravimetric capacity of 3.07 wt% and a volumetric capacity of 79.65 g & sdot;H2/L.
Additionally, the estimated desorption temperature of approximately 612.69 K indicates favorable conditions for the practical release of hydrogen from NaGeH3.
The calculated elastic constants (C11 = 69.55 GPa, C12 = 18.06 GPa, C44 = 6.93 GPa) satisfy Born's stability criteria for cubic crystals.

The analysis of mechanical properties, including Pugh's ratio (B/G), anisotropy factor (A), and Poisson's ratio (nu), confirms that the material exhibits ductility, anisotropy, and a predominantly ionic bonding nature.
The calculated melting point of 964.01 K indicates good thermal stability.
Moreover, the electronic structure analysis indicates that NaGeH3 displays metallic behavior, with a noticeable density of states at the Fermi level primarily contributed by Ge-p orbitals.

Although its high electrical and thermal conductivities may reduce its thermoelectric efficiency, these properties are advantageous for hydrogen storage, as they facilitate effective heat dissipation and charge transport.
Accordingly, NaGeH3 exhibits promising characteristics, making it an attractive candidate for hydrogen storage systems.
